claude.sample_unit: hospitalized patients labeled with AKI by standard KDIGO criteria
unlisted_practices: Refining AKI outcome labeling criteria (excluding transient creatinine decreases, minimum absolute creatinine increase) to improve prognostic validity and ML model performance
Dual-alert clinical decision support distinguishing refined AKI from ambiguous AKI cases

links.effect: 978/5,115 (19.1%) standard KDIGO-labeled patients were considered ambiguous; 4,137 (80.9%) met refined criteria.
links.quote: Among 5,115 patients labeled by the standard KDIGO, 4,137 (80.9%) met the refined criteria, and 978 (19.1%) were considered ambiguous.

links.outcome: Model discrimination, precision, and false-positive alerts
links.effect: Refined-label models: AUROC 0.935 vs. 0.926; AUPRC 0.729 vs. 0.707; 27% fewer false-positive alerts, with minimal detection loss.
links.quote: ML models trained with refined labels showed improved discrimination (AUROC, 0.935 vs. 0.926) and precision (AUPRC, 0.729 vs. 0.707) and reduced false-positive alerts by 27% with minimal loss in adverse outcome detection.

unlisted_practices: Refine AKI labels by excluding transient serum creatinine decreases from baseline estimation and applying a minimum absolute serum creatinine increase threshold.
Use a dual-alert clinical decision support system to distinguish refined AKI from ambiguous AKI cases.
Refining algorithmic ground-truth labeling criteria (e.g., baseline serum creatinine estimation and minimum absolute increase thresholds) to train and evaluate predictive models
Employing a dual-alert clinical decision support architecture to distinguish definite condition cases from ambiguous cases
